cls: Angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) - selective AT1 antagonist
quick: May be taken with or without food, consistently
CONTRAINDICATED - drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system cause fetal injury/death (boxed warning); stop as soon as pregnancy is detected
Not recommended; no human milk data, potential infant harm
No initial adjustment if CrCl >=30; caution and monitor in severe impairment; avoid in renal artery stenosis
Use caution; consider lower dose in biliary obstruction / hepatic impairment
Blood pressure, serum potassium, renal function (creatinine)
summary: Valsartan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that selectively blocks the AT1 receptor, lowering blood pressure independent of angiotensin II synthesis and without affecting bradykinin (so less cough than ACE inhibitors). It is used for hypertension, heart failure (NYHA II-IV), and to reduce cardiovascular mortality after myocardial infarction. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and must be stopped when pregnancy is detected.
indications: Hypertension in adults and children >=6 years
Heart failure (NYHA class II-IV) - reduces hospitalization for heart failure
Post-myocardial infarction - reduction of cardiovascular mortality in stable patients with left ventricular failure or dysfunction

dosage.d: 80 or 160 mg once daily; range 80-320 mg once daily
dosage.n: Max effect by ~4 weeks; add a diuretic for greater effect

dosage.d: 40 mg twice daily, titrate to 80-160 mg twice daily as tolerated
dosage.n: Target 160 mg twice daily; uptitrate gradually

dosage.d: 20 mg twice daily, titrate up to 160 mg twice daily as tolerated
dosage.n: Start as early as 12 h post-MI; titrate over weeks

dosage.d: 1 mg/kg once daily (up to 40 mg); range 1-4 mg/kg (up to 160 mg)
dosage.n: Tablets and suspension are not mg-for-mg interchangeable

admin: Take once or twice daily at the same time(s) each day, with or without food
Tablets and the oral suspension are NOT interchangeable on a mg-per-mg basis (suspension AUC ~60% higher)
Correct volume depletion before starting in volume-depleted patients to avoid hypotension
Do not combine with an ACE inhibitor or aliskiren (in diabetics) for dual RAS blockade
Continue taking even when feeling well; do not stop abruptly without medical advice
moa: Valsartan selectively blocks the binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor in vascular smooth muscle and the adrenal gland, antagonizing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone release. Its action is independent of the pathway of angiotensin II synthesis. Unlike ACE inhibitors it does not inhibit ACE (kininase II), so it does not raise bradykinin and causes less cough.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to valsartan or any component
Concomitant aliskiren in patients with diabetes
relative: Volume- or salt-depleted patients (risk of symptomatic hypotension)

preg: CONTRAINDICATED. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. Use in the second and third trimesters reduces fetal renal function and increases fetal/neonatal morbidity and death (oligohydramnios, anuria, renal failure, lung hypoplasia, skull hypoplasia, hypotension). When pregnancy is detected, discontinue valsartan as soon as possible and switch to an alternative agent. Monitor exposed neonates for hypotension, oliguria, and hyperkalemia.
lact: There is no information on the presence of valsartan in human milk. Because of the potential for adverse effects on the nursing infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during valsartan therapy.
renal: No initial dosage adjustment is needed for mild-to-moderate impairment (CrCl >=30 mL/min). Use with caution and monitor in severe renal impairment; avoid in bilateral renal artery stenosis. Valsartan is not removed by hemodialysis. Monitor potassium and creatinine closely.
hepatic: Use with caution; consider a lower dose in patients with mild-to-moderate hepatic impairment or biliary-obstructive disorders, as exposure is increased. Not studied adequately in severe hepatic impairment.

major: Aliskiren in patients with diabetes (contraindicated) - hyperkalemia, renal impairment, hypotension
ACE inhibitors / dual RAS blockade - increased hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal failure (avoid)
moderate: Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes, heparin (hyperkalemia)
NSAIDs/COX-2 inhibitors (reduced antihypertensive effect; renal impairment, especially in elderly/volume-depleted)
Lithium (increased serum lithium and toxicity - monitor levels)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food
interactions.diagnostics: May raise serum potassium and creatinine; monitor electrolytes and renal function

serious: Acute renal failure / worsening renal function
rare: Angioedema (swelling of face, lips, tongue, throat)

monitoring: Serum potassium (especially with other RAS blockers, K-sparing diuretics, or renal impairment)
Renal function / serum creatinine (after initiation and dose changes, particularly in heart failure)
Signs of hypotension in volume-depleted or heart-failure patients
Pregnancy status in women of childbearing potential
counsel: Tell your doctor immediately if you are or may become pregnant - this medicine can harm the developing baby and must be stopped
Take it at the same time each day; do not stop suddenly without talking to your doctor
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless your doctor approves
Rise slowly from sitting or lying to reduce dizziness, and report fainting, very high heart rate, or swelling of the face/lips/tongue
Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) without medical advice, as they can reduce the effect and harm the kidneys
pk: Antihypertensive effect begins within 2 hours; substantial within 2 weeks
Plasma peak approximately 2 to 4 hours; maximal blood-pressure effect by ~4 weeks
Antihypertensive effect persists over 24 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); protect from moisture; dispense in a tight container
pearls: BOXED WARNING: fetal toxicity - stop as soon as pregnancy is detected; avoid in any woman planning pregnancy
ARBs cause far less dry cough and angioedema than ACE inhibitors (no bradykinin accumulation)
Avoid dual RAS blockade (with ACE inhibitor or aliskiren) - increases hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal failure without added benefit
Tablets and oral suspension are NOT mg-for-mg interchangeable (suspension exposure ~60% higher)
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your normal schedule - do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Overdose most likely causes marked hypotension and tachycardia; bradycardia may occur from vagal stimulation, and depressed consciousness, circulatory collapse, and shock have been reported. Management is supportive - place the patient supine and give intravenous fluids/volume expansion for hypotension. Valsartan is not removed by hemodialysis because of high protein binding.
